mainTopic: The צרה of a כהן גדול's widowed יבמה; the sources and rabbinic status of שניות; the ברייתא's list of שניות; and which שניות have a הפסק
overview: The amud opens by settling an earlier dispute about a widow who falls to a כהן גדול for יבום, and whether that frees her צרה. The dispute is narrowed to a widow from אירוסין. The view that she does not free the צרה is refuted by a ברייתא, and ריש לקיש is defended, since חליצה in place of יבום is not the מצוה. רבא then finds a hint in the תורה for שניות, the rabbinic secondary forbidden relationships. This leads to a side discussion with רבי לוי about why cheating with measures is harsher than עריות: it cannot be fully fixed with תשובה. רב יהודה, רבי אושעיא and רב כהנא each offer another source for making a fence around עריות, and the גמרא concludes that שניות are rabbinic and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא. A ברייתא then lists the שניות and some stepfamily cases, and the גמרא explains its wording. Finally, רב and זעירי discuss which שניות have a הפסק, a point where the prohibition stops, and the גמרא begins to look at the daughter-in-law case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A widow after full marriage: everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: If the widow had a full marriage (נישואין) with the dead brother, everyone agrees her coming to the כהן גדול does not free the צרה, because an עשה cannot push aside a לא תעשה plus an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a widow from full marriage, everyone agrees she does not free the other wife, because a positive command cannot override a prohibition that also comes with a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts narrowing an earlier dispute. It first marks off a case where there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow after נישואין is forbidden to a כהן גדול by two commands: the לאו against marrying a widow, and the עשה to marry a בתולה. The מצוה of יבום is only one עשה, so it cannot beat a לאו and an עשה together. Since the יבום has no power here, it cannot free the צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died after full marriage (not just engagement)
Everyone agrees; there is no argument here
Frees, meaning frees the צרה from יבום

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: A positive command does not push aside a prohibition that also has a positive command attached

phrases.english: With a widow from full marriage —

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא פָּטְרָה,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that she does not free [the other wife],

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה.
phrases.english: because a positive command does not override a prohibition plus a positive command.
phrases.notes: The extra עשה is the כהן גדול's command to marry a בתולה, and a fully married widow is not one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an earlier discussion; marks off the case with no argument
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow from נישואין falling to a כהן גדול does not free her צרה, since one עשה cannot override a לאו and an עשה together.

steps.title: The real argument: a widow from engagement
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is only about a widow from אירוסין. One side says the עשה of יבום overrides the לאו, so she frees the צרה. The other side says it does not, because חליצה is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about a widow from engagement. The one who says she frees the other wife holds that the positive command comes and overrides the prohibition. The one who says she does not free her holds that the positive command does not override the prohibition, since חליצה is possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the exact case where the two opinions argue and gives the reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow from אירוסין is still a בתולה, so only the לאו against a widow applies. One side says the normal rule, עשה דוחה לא תעשה, works here, so the יבום counts and frees the צרה. The other side says an עשה only overrides a לאו when there is no other way, and here there is another way: חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died after engagement but before full marriage
A positive command comes and pushes aside a prohibition
Since it is possible (to do it another way)
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום without marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that עשה דוחה לא תעשה is a real rule. They only argue whether it still applies when there is another way, here חליצה, that avoids the לאו.

phrases.english: Where they argue is with a widow from engagement.
The one who says she frees [the other wife] —

phrases.aramaic: אָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: [holds that] the positive command comes and overrides the prohibition.
And the one who says she does not free her —

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: [holds that] the positive command does not come and override the prohibition,
since it is possible [to use] חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having marked off the agreed case, now defines the case in dispute and both reasons
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a widow from אירוסין, one view says the עשה of יבום overrides the לאו and frees the צרה; the other says it does not, since חליצה is possible.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא: if they had relations, they acquired her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that she does not free the צרה, using a ברייתא that says if such a forbidden יבם had relations with her, he acquired her.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: but [the ברייתא says] if they had relations, they acquired her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second opinion, 'she does not free the צרה', with an earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that even when יבום is forbidden by a לאו, the act still works and the יבם acquires her. If the act works, it should also free the צרה. That goes against the view that the כהן גדול's act does not free her.

keyTerms.meaning: They acquired her as a wife

phrases.english: They challenged: and if they had relations, they acquired her!
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא brought earlier about יבמים who are forbidden to do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'does not free' opinion from step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the widow from אירוסין does not free her צרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows a forbidden act of יבום still acquires. A valid יבום should free the צרה.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the challenge is a full refutation. The view that she does not free the צרה is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא knocks out the 'does not free' opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered, so that opinion falls. What remains is that the act of יבום with a widow from אירוסין does work and frees the צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the opinion is rejected

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 3 with no answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The opinion that a widow from אירוסין does not free her צרה is rejected.

steps.title: Is ריש לקיש refuted too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this refutation also knocks out ריש לקיש, whose rule is that when both an עשה and a לאו can be kept, the עשה does not override.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is also a refutation of ריש לקיש?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether ריש לקיש falls together with the opinion just rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejected opinion relied on 'since חליצה is possible', which sounds like ריש לקיש's rule: if you can keep both the עשה and the לא תעשה, do that, and the עשה does not override. If that reasoning was refuted, maybe ריש לקיש's rule is refuted as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (often opens a suggestion the גמרא will test)

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא תִּיהְוֵי נָמֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ?!
phrases.english: Shall we say this is also a refutation of ריש לקיש?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תִּיהְוֵי נָמֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the refutation of step 4 to ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that an עשה does not override a לאו when both can be kept
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The refuted reasoning ('since חליצה is possible') is the same as ריש לקיש's rule, so the refutation should reach him too.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: חליצה instead of יבום is not the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that his rule only applies when the other way still fulfills the מצוה. Doing חליצה where יבום is possible does not count as that מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can tell you: when I said my rule, it was where the מצוה is still fulfilled. But here, חליצה in place of יבום is not the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by limiting his rule to a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule says to keep both the עשה and the לאו when you can, but only if the other path still fulfills the מצוה. חליצה in place of יבום is not doing the מצוה of יבום, so 'חליצה is possible' does not count as keeping both. That is why the refutation of that reasoning does not touch ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He could tell you (a defense of someone's opinion)
In place of יבום, where יבום could have been done

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule only applies when the other path still fulfills the מצוה. חליצה where יבום is possible is not the מצוה, so his rule stands.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש can tell you:
When I said [my rule] —
it was where the מצוה is fulfilled,
but here, חליצה in place of יבום —
is not the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's rule seemed to cover any case where another path avoids the לאו, including חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule only applies when the other path still fulfills the מצוה. חליצה in place of יבום does not, so he is not refuted.

steps.title: רבא: a hint in the תורה for שניות
steps.stepSummary: רבא finds a hint for שניות in the פסוק 'כי את כל התועבות האל'. The word 'האל' means the harsh ones, which implies there are also soft ones, and those are the שניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: where is the hint in the תורה for secondary forbidden relationships? As it says: 'For all these abominations the men of the land did.' 'These' means the harsh ones, which implies there are soft ones. What are they? The secondary relationships.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא shows that the רבנן's lesser forbidden relationships have a hint in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the short form 'האל' for 'these', and רבא reads it as 'the harsh ones', the תורה's own forbidden relationships. Calling some 'harsh' implies there are also 'soft' ones, and רבא says those are the שניות. They are still rabbinic, but this gives them a hint in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint, not a full source
Secondary forbidden relationships set by the רבנן
Harsh ones, the severe forbidden relationships
Soft ones, the lighter forbidden relationships

steps.confusionAlert: A רמז is not a תורה law. The שניות stay rabbinic; רבא only shows the תורה hints at them.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads 'האל' as 'the harsh ones', which implies 'soft ones', the rabbinic שניות.

phrases.english: רבא said:
From where is there a hint in the תורה for secondary relationships?
As it says: 'For all these abominations'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:27

phrases.english: the men of the land did,'
'These' means the harsh ones,
which implies there are soft ones,
and what are they? The secondary relationships.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רֶמֶז לִשְׁנִיּוֹת מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the source for שניות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שניות are hinted at in the תורה: 'האל' means harsh ones, which implies soft ones, and those are the שניות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It opens the גמרא's long discussion of which relatives count as שניות, and shows the רבנן's laws are tied to a hint in the תורה.

steps.title: How do we know 'האל' means harsh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the word 'האל' carries the meaning 'harsh'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that 'האל' is a word that means 'harsh'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבא knew that 'האל' means 'harsh'. This sets up the next line, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's whole hint for שניות depended on reading 'האל' as 'the harsh ones'. Normally 'האל' just means 'these', so the גמרא wants proof of this second meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied? What shows this?
'These', which can also hint at 'the harsh/strong ones'

phrases.english: And what shows
that 'האל' is a word meaning harsh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the word-meaning that רבא used in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source proving that 'האל' can mean 'harsh/strong'.

steps.title: Proof from 'the mighty of the land'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in יחזקאל where 'אילי' means the mighty, strong people of the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the mighty ones (אילי) of the land he took away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק in which the same root, 'אֵל', refers to strong, powerful people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, 'אילי הארץ' means the strong leaders of the land. Since 'האל' shares this root, it can carry the sense of 'strong' or 'harsh'. That supports רבא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The mighty, powerful ones of the land

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the mighty of the land he took.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 17:13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The root 'אל' means 'mighty' in יחזקאל, so 'האל' can mean 'harsh'.

steps.title: Does this clash with רבי לוי?
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי said that 'אלה' (used for cheating with measures) shows harshness, while 'אל' (used for עריות) shows less harshness. This seems to clash with reading 'האל' as harsh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this argues with רבי לוי? רבי לוי said: the punishment for dishonest measures is harsher than the punishment for עריות. For עריות the Torah says 'אל', and for measures it says 'אלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא worries that רבא's reading goes against רבי לוי. רבי לוי treated 'אלה' as the harsh word, and 'אל' as the milder one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי learned that cheating with measures is worse than עריות, because measures got the longer word 'אלה' and עריות only got 'אל'. That seems to mean 'אל' is NOT the harsh word. But רבא just read 'האל' by עריות as 'the harsh ones'.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it argues with…?
Measures (here: cheating with weights and measures)

phrases.english: Shall we say it argues with רבי לוי?
For רבי לוי said:
The punishment for dishonest measures is harsher
than the punishment for forbidden relationships,
for about these (עריות) it says 'אל',
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is עריות, where ויקרא 18:27 says 'האל'.

phrases.english: and about those (measures) it says 'אלה'!
phrases.notes: That's from דברים 25:16: 'כל עשה אלה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's reading of 'האל' against another אמורא's teaching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי לוי uses 'אלה' as the sign of harshness and 'אל' as the milder word, which seems to deny that 'אל' means harsh.

steps.title: Both are harsh, but 'אלה' is harsher
steps.stepSummary: There is no argument: 'אל' means harsh, and 'אלה' means even harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'אל' means harsh, and 'אלה' means harsher than 'אל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא and רבי לוי can both be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי never said 'אל' isn't harsh. He only said 'אלה' is harsher still. So עריות are harsh (good for רבא), and measures are even harsher (good for רבי לוי).

keyTerms.meaning: 'These', the longer form, read as even harsher

phrases.english: 'אל' is harsh,
and 'אלה' is harsher than 'אל'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization by levels: both words mean harsh, to different degrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי לוי treats 'אל' as not harsh at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אל' is harsh and 'אלה' is harsher, so the two views fit together.

steps.title: But עריות also have the word 'אלה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that by עריות the Torah also says 'אלה', so why should measures be harsher?
steps.simpleTranslation: But by עריות it also says 'אלה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי לוי's proof. The same 'harsher' word, 'אלה', also appears by עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אלה' shows extra harshness, then עריות should be just as harsh as measures. So the comparison seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: By forbidden relationships too
it is written 'אלה'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29: 'כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבת האלה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the basis of רבי לוי's comparison, now that it has been accepted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי לוי's proof that measures are harsher than עריות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אלה' also appears by עריות, so the word cannot show that measures are harsher.

steps.title: That 'אלה' keeps measures out of כרת
steps.stepSummary: The 'אלה' by עריות is not about harshness. It teaches that only 'these' sins get כרת, which leaves out cheating with measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to exclude measures from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'אלה' by עריות has a different job. It does not show harshness there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק by עריות says 'these' are punished with כרת. That limits כרת to these sins and excludes measures. So that 'אלה' is used up for this teaching, and it says nothing about how harsh עריות are.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: measures do NOT get כרת. Yet רבי לוי still calls their punishment harsher. The next steps explain how.

phrases.english: That one is to exclude measures from כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is used for a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אלה' by עריות shows that עריות are extra harsh.
steps.terutzMaskana: That 'אלה' limits כרת to עריות and leaves out measures.

steps.title: So what makes measures more severe?
steps.stepSummary: Measures don't get כרת, so the גמרא asks in what way they are harsher than עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is their greater severity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a natural follow-up. If cheating with measures has no כרת, how can it be worse? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 just showed that עריות carry כרת and measures do not. That seems to make עריות the more severe sin, so רבי לוי's 'harsher' needs a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Their severity, what makes them stricter

phrases.english: Rather, what is their severity?
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the sin of cheating with measures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 13, which removed כרת from measures.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way the sin of measures is harsher than עריות.

steps.title: עריות can be fixed with תשובה, measures cannot
steps.stepSummary: Someone who sinned with עריות can do תשובה. Someone who cheated with measures cannot fully do תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These (עריות) can be fixed by תשובה; those (measures) cannot be fixed by תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the extra severity of measures is about fixing the sin, not about the punishment's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עריות, the sinner can do תשובה. The usual explanation for measures is this: the cheater has taken small amounts from many unknown customers. He cannot find them all to pay them back, so he cannot fully repent.
steps.whatToRemember: 'האל' means harsh (from 'אילי הארץ'). 'אלה' is even harsher. The 'אלה' by עריות excludes measures from כרת. Measures are still worse in one way, because the sinner cannot fully do תשובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a sin can be 'harsher' even without a heavier punishment, if it is one that can hardly be repaired.

phrases.english: These — can be fixed through repentance,
phrases.notes: The first 'these' are עריות; the second 'these' are the cheaters with measures.

phrases.english: those — cannot be fixed through repentance.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי — אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְשׁוּבָה, הָנֵי — לָא אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14 and closes the discussion of רבי לוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Measures are more severe because they cannot be fully repaired through תשובה, while עריות can.

steps.title: רב יהודה's source: שלמה made handles for the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה learns the idea of שניות from a פסוק in קהלת saying that שלמה 'weighed' (אִזֵּן). עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר explains that שלמה made 'handles' (אׇזְנַיִם) for the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: we learn it from here: 'He weighed and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.' And עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: before שלמה came, the תורה was like a basket with no handles, until שלמה came and made handles for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another source for the rabbinic fence of שניות. רב יהודה points to a פסוק about שלמה, and a teaching of רבי אלעזר explains what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אִזֵּן sounds like אׇזְנַיִם, meaning handles. A basket without handles is hard to grab and carry. Fences like שניות are 'handles' that make the תורה easier to hold onto, so people do not slip into real עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary forbidden relationships, forbidden by the רבנן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שלמה changed the תורה. The 'handles' are protective rules that help people keep the תורה; the תורה itself stays the same.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: from here:
"He weighed and sought out, and set in order many proverbs"
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:9. Keep your eye on the word וְאִזֵּן; it sounds like the word for handles.

phrases.english: And Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
Before Solomon came,
the Torah was like a basket
that has no handles,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא שְׁלֹמֹה וְעָשָׂה לָהּ אׇזְנַיִם.
phrases.english: until Solomon came and made handles for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about measures and עריות, returns to רבא's question from step 7 and offers a different source for שניות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 12:9, explained by רבי אלעזר as שלמה making 'handles' for the תורה

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's source: stay far away from sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא learns the idea of שניות from a פסוק in משלי that tells a person to keep away from sin and not even pass near it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: we learn it from here: 'Avoid it, do not pass by it; turn away from it and pass on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source for שניות. רבי אושעיא uses a פסוק that tells us to keep a distance from sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not only say 'don't do it.' It says don't even come near it. That is exactly what שניות are: keeping a person away from the area around the real עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: Avoid it, keep away from it

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said: from here:
"Avoid it, do not pass by it;
phrases.notes: משלי 4:15

phrases.english: turn from it and pass on."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the same idea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 4:15, which tells a person to stay far from sin

steps.title: רב אשי's parable of guarding an orchard
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains רבי אושעיא with a parable: a guard standing outside the orchard protects all of it, but a guard standing inside only protects what is in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: what is רבי אושעיא's idea like? Like a man guarding an orchard. If he guards it from the outside, the whole orchard is guarded. If he guards it from the inside, what is in front of him is guarded, but what is behind him is not guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a picture to explain why we should guard from the outside, like רבי אושעיא said. This parable sets up the גמרא's next move, which will criticize it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Guarding from the outside means having a fence (שניות) before you even reach the real sin. Guarding from the inside means only watching yourself once you are already close. According to the parable, the outside guard is simply better because it covers more.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה —
phrases.english: A parable for Rabbi Oshaya's idea: what is it like?
To a man guarding an orchard.
If he guards it from the outside, all of it is guarded.
If he guards it from the inside,
what is in front of him is guarded,
what is behind him is not guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי אושעיא's source with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guarding from the outside protects everything; guarding from the inside protects only part.

steps.title: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's parable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב אשי's parable is not accurate. In an orchard, guarding from inside still protects part of it. But with עריות, without the fence of שניות a person would end up sinning with the real ערוה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this parable of רב אשי is a mistake. There, in the orchard, at least what is in front of him is guarded. Here, if not for the שניות, he would run right into the ערוה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי's parable and says it makes the fence sound less important than it really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parable suggests that without the outside guard you still keep part of the orchard safe. With עריות, there is no 'partly safe': without שניות a person would fall into the actual sin. So the fence is not just better, it is necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, something made up and not accurate

steps.whatToRemember: The fence of שניות is not just extra credit. According to the גמרא, without it a person would end up doing the real איסור.

phrases.english: But this of Rav Ashi is a mistake.
There, at least what is in front of him is guarded.
phrases.notes: "There" means the orchard in רב אשי's parable.

phrases.english: Here, if not for the secondary relationships,
he would run into the forbidden relationship itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the parable given in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אשי's parable is rejected, not רבי אושעיא's source itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The parable implies that guarding from inside still protects part; but with עריות, no fence means falling into the real sin.

steps.title: רב כהנא's source: make a guard for My guard
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns the idea of שניות from a פסוק in the תורה about עריות: 'You shall guard My guard,' meaning make a protective guard around what the תורה forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: we learn it from here: 'You shall keep My charge.' This means: make a guard for My guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more source for שניות, this time from a פסוק in the תורה itself, at the end of the פרשה of עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses a double word: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם and מִשְׁמַרְתִּי. רב כהנא reads this as 'put a guard around My guard,' meaning the רבנן should add a fence around the תורה's עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: My charge, what I command you to guard

steps.whatToRemember: All these sources (רב יהודה, רבי אושעיא, רב כהנא) point to the same idea: the רבנן may add a fence like שניות to protect people from real עריות.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: from here:
"You shall keep My charge"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:30

phrases.english: make a guard for My charge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion of רב אשי's parable, the גמרא returns to listing sources and gives another one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 18:30, read as 'make a guard for My guard'

steps.title: If a פסוק is the source, שניות would be Torah law
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף: רב כהנא's proof from a פסוק would make שניות Torah law, but they are only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: But this would make it Torah law!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב כהנא's proof from the last step. If שניות come from a פסוק, they would be Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that שניות are a rabbinic prohibition. So a source that seems to make them Torah law cannot be right as it stands. The problem is not the idea of a fence, but what level of law it is.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
But this is Torah law!
phrases.notes: He means: learning שניות from a פסוק would turn them into Torah law, and we know they are rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב כהנא's proof from 'ושמרתם את משמרתי'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's use of 'ושמרתם את משמרתי' as the source for שניות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real Torah source would make שניות Torah law, but they are known to be rabbinic.

steps.title: The תורה commands it and the רבנן explain it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers: the command to make a fence is from the תורה, and the רבנן filled in the details.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is Torah law, and the Sages explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends the proof. The Torah gave a general order to make a fence, and the Sages decided which relatives it covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tries to keep the פסוק as a real source. It explains why the list feels rabbinic: the details come from the Sages, even though the basic command is from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages explained it; they spelled out the details

phrases.english: It is Torah law,
and the Sages explained it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the law: a Torah-level command with rabbinic details.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסוק source means the whole law is fully Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah gives the general command, and the Sages define its scope.

steps.title: The רבנן explain the whole תורה too
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: the רבנן explain all of the תורה, and it is still Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages explained the whole Torah too!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's answer. Explaining a Torah law does not make it rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Almost every Torah law is explained by the Sages, and it stays Torah law. So 'the Sages explained it' does not lower שניות to rabbinic level. The original problem comes back.

phrases.english: The whole Torah too
the Sages explained!
phrases.notes: And yet all of it is still Torah law. So this answer doesn't make שניות rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that rabbinic explanation makes the law feel rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rabbinic explanation applies to all Torah laws, and they stay Torah law.

steps.title: שניות are rabbinic, and the פסוק is only a hint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שניות are a rabbinic law and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: it is rabbinic, and the verse is merely a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question. שניות are a rabbinic law, and the פסוק is only a hint the Sages attached to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a פסוק used as a reminder or support for a rabbinic rule, not as its real source. So all the פסוקים brought for שניות are hints, and the law is fully rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק used only as a support or hint for a rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: שניות are rabbinic. The פסוק 'ושמרתם את משמרתי' is only an אסמכתא, a hint, not a true Torah source.
steps.confusionAlert: An אסמכתא does not make a law Torah law. The פסוק is quoted, but the prohibition is still only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Rather: it is rabbinic,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a final answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שניות are a rabbinic prohibition; the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא's list of שניות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists which relatives count as שניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: What are the secondary relationships? His mother's mother, his father's mother, his father's father's wife, his mother's father's wife, the wife of his father's brother from the same mother, the wife of his mother's brother from the same father, his son's daughter-in-law, and his daughter's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists the relatives forbidden as שניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are relatives one step beyond the Torah's עריות. For example, the Torah forbids a father's brother's wife when the brothers share a father, so the Sages added the brother who shares only a mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary forbidden relatives, forbidden by the Sages

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What are the secondary relationships?
His mother's mother, and his father's mother,
and his father's father's wife,
and his mother's father's wife,
and the wife of his father's brother from the same mother,
and the wife of his mother's brother from the same father,
and his son's daughter-in-law, and his daughter's daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After deciding that שניות are rabbinic, the גמרא lists them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight relatives are listed as שניות.

steps.title: Who is permitted and who is forbidden in stepfamily cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a father-in-law's wife and a stepson's wife are permitted, but a stepson's daughter is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man is permitted to his father-in-law's wife and to his stepson's wife, but forbidden to his stepson's daughter. And his stepson is permitted to his wife and his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now tells us which relatives the Sages did not forbid, plus one who is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages did not extend שניות to every in-law. A father-in-law's other wife (not the mother-in-law) and a stepson's ex-wife are allowed. A stepson's daughter is forbidden, which the גמרא will soon question.

phrases.english: And a man is permitted to his father-in-law's wife
phrases.notes: This means another wife of his father-in-law, not his own wife's mother.

phrases.english: and to his stepson's wife,
and he is forbidden to his stepson's daughter.
And his stepson is permitted to his wife and his daughter.
phrases.notes: The stepfather's wife here is another wife, not the stepson's own mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with permitted cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father-in-law's wife and a stepson's wife are permitted; a stepson's daughter is forbidden; a stepson may marry his stepfather's wife and daughter.

steps.title: "I am permitted to you, but my daughter is forbidden"
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out a strange result: the stepson's wife is permitted to the stepfather, but her daughter is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his stepson's wife says to him: I am permitted to you, but my daughter is forbidden to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes an odd situation that comes out of the rules it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you would expect the mother to be more forbidden than her daughter. Here it is the opposite: the stepson's wife is allowed, while her daughter, who is the stepson's daughter, is forbidden.

phrases.english: And his stepson's wife says to him:
"I am permitted to you,
but my daughter is forbidden to you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an unusual result from the rules in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stepson's wife is permitted to the stepfather, while her daughter is forbidden.

steps.title: A stepson's daughter is forbidden by the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a stepson's daughter is in a ברייתא about שניות when the Torah already forbids her.
steps.simpleTranslation: His stepson's daughter is forbidden by Torah law, as it is written: "her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. A stepson's daughter is not a rabbinic שניה; the Torah itself forbids her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stepson is his wife's son, so the stepson's daughter is his wife's son's daughter. The Torah forbids that relative explicitly. So why is she in a list of rabbinic prohibitions?

phrases.english: His stepson's daughter is forbidden by Torah law,
as it is written:
"her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17. 'Her' is his wife, so her son's daughter is his stepson's daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one item from the ברייתא's rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of a stepson's daughter among rabbinic cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is already forbidden by an explicit פסוק, so she does not belong in a list of rabbinic prohibitions.

steps.title: She was listed only to set up the later line
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentioned the stepson's daughter only so it could teach the contrast in the later line.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it wanted to teach the end part: His stepson's wife says to him, "I am permitted to you and my daughter is forbidden to you." And even though my daughter is forbidden to you by Torah law, regarding me the Sages did not make a decree. So it also taught his stepson's daughter in the first part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the stepson's daughter is not being called a rabbinic שניה. She was mentioned to prepare for the later line about her mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the later line is that the Sages did not forbid the mother, even though her daughter is forbidden by the Torah. To set up that contrast, the first part had to mention the daughter. Her prohibition is still Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching

steps.whatToRemember: A stepson's daughter is forbidden by the Torah. The ברייתא lists her only to set up the line about the stepson's wife, whom the Sages did not forbid.

phrases.english: Because it wanted to teach the end part:
His stepson's wife says to him:
"I am permitted to you
and my daughter is forbidden to you,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּבִתִּי אֲסוּרָה לְךָ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: and even though my daughter is forbidden to you by Torah law,
regarding me the Sages did not make a decree,
so it also taught his stepson's daughter in the first part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the stepson's daughter.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the style of the teaching: an item is listed to set up a later line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls the stepson's daughter a rabbinic שניה.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is forbidden by the Torah and is mentioned only to set up the contrast with her mother, whom the Sages did not forbid.

steps.title: Why not also teach the father-in-law's wife case?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא wanted to show a strange 'she is permitted but her daughter is forbidden' result, it could also have used the father-in-law's wife, whose daughter is the man's wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then say the same about his father-in-law's wife: 'I am permitted to you, but my daughter is forbidden to you,' because her daughter is his wife's sister!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 29. If the ברייתא brought the stepson's daughter just to show a strange contrast, it should have shown the same contrast with the father-in-law's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (step 26) already said that the father-in-law's wife is permitted. Her daughter is his wife's sister, and she is forbidden. So the same 'mother permitted, daughter forbidden' pattern exists here too, and the ברייתא should have pointed it out.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your explanation is right
His father-in-law's wife (not his wife's mother)

phrases.english: If so,
let it also say about his father-in-law's wife:
phrases.notes: This is a wife of the father-in-law who is not the mother of his wife, so she is permitted.

phrases.english: I am permitted to you
and my daughter is forbidden to you,
since she is his wife's sister!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵשֶׁת חָמִיו נָמֵי תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 29 about why the ברייתא mentioned the stepson's daughter.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא listed the stepson's daughter only to teach the strange contrast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goal was to teach the contrast, a matching case (the father-in-law's wife and her daughter) should also have been taught.

steps.title: One case is permanent, the other is not
steps.stepSummary: The stepson case is fixed forever. The father-in-law case can change, because his wife's sister becomes permitted after his wife dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is fixed for him; that one is not fixed for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only teaches the contrast where it is permanent. The stepson's daughter is forbidden forever, but the wife's sister is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's sister is forbidden only while the wife is alive. Once his wife dies, he may marry her sister. So the 'daughter forbidden' half of the father-in-law case is not a lasting contrast, and the ברייתא did not bother to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed, settled, the same in every situation

phrases.english: This one is fixed for him,
phrases.notes: The stepson's wife is always permitted and her daughter is always forbidden.

phrases.english: that one is not fixed for him.
phrases.notes: His wife's sister is forbidden only while his wife is alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ, הָא לָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: permanent versus temporary prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father-in-law's wife case is the same kind of contrast and should have been listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only lists a contrast that holds forever. The wife's sister is forbidden only temporarily.

steps.title: רב: four women whose prohibition stops
steps.stepSummary: רב says that four kinds of שניות have a הפסק, a stopping point. He remembered three: the wife of his mother's paternal half-brother, the wife of his father's maternal half-brother, and his daughter-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Four women have a stopping point. רב held three of them in his hand: the wife of his mother's brother from the father's side, the wife of his father's brother from the mother's side, and his daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a tradition that for four kinds of שניות, the רבנן's prohibition stops and does not reach further generations, and he lists the three he remembered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many שניות continue up or down the generations, for example the wife of a grandfather's father. For these four, the prohibition applies only to the woman named and does not continue. רב was sure about three of the four.

keyTerms.meaning: A stopping point: the prohibition does not continue to further generations
Held in his hand: he remembered it for sure
The wife of his mother's brother who shares only her father
The wife of his father's brother who shares only his mother

phrases.english: Rav said,
four women have a stopping point.
phrases.notes: Their prohibition is only for the woman named. It doesn't continue to further generations.

phrases.english: Rav held three of them in his hand:
the wife of the mother's brother from the father,
and the wife of the father's brother from the mother,
and his daughter-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב, אַרְבַּע נָשִׁים יֵשׁ לָהֶן הֶפְסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's list of שניות to a new rule about which שניות stop and do not continue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four kinds of שניות have a הפסק. רב knew three: the wife of his mother's paternal half-brother, the wife of his father's maternal half-brother, and his daughter-in-law.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that not every שניה works the same way. Some continue through the generations and some stop.

steps.title: זעירי adds the fourth: his mother's father's wife
steps.stepSummary: זעירי completes the list of four by adding the wife of his mother's father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And זעירי adds: also the wife of his mother's father.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי gives the missing fourth case that רב did not remember.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife of his mother's father (not his own grandmother) is a שניה. According to זעירי, her prohibition stops there and does not continue to the wives of the ancestors further up the mother's father's line.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of his mother's father

phrases.english: And Ze'eiri adds
also the wife of his mother's father.
phrases.notes: This is a wife of his maternal grandfather who is not his own grandmother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּזְעֵירִי מוֹסִיף אַף אֵשֶׁת אֲבִי אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the fourth item that רב was missing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife of his mother's father also has a הפסק.

steps.title: A memory aid for זעירי's addition
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a sign: זעירי's case is 'on top of רב', one generation higher than רב's cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: And your sign is: 'the one above, of רב.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a short memory trick so we remember which case זעירי added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's cases are uncles' wives and a daughter-in-law. זעירי's case, the mother's father's wife, reaches one generation higher. The word עילאי, 'upper', hints that זעירי added the case above רב's.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said,
and your sign is:
the upper one, on top of Rav's.
phrases.notes: זעירי added a case one generation higher than רב's list: the grandfather's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְסִימָנָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way to remember the addition from step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Memory aid: זעירי's added case is the 'upper' one, above רב's cases.

steps.title: Why רב did not count the mother's father's wife
steps.stepSummary: רב did not count it because people might mix it up with the father's father's wife, whose prohibition does continue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason רב did not count it? Because it could be confused with the wife of his father's father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב left out זעירי's case, and it answers that רב feared people would confuse it with a similar case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of a father's wife continues up through all the fathers' fathers. A mother's father's wife looks very similar. So to prevent mistakes, the רבנן also let her prohibition continue upward, and for רב she has no הפסק.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of his father's father

phrases.english: And what is the reason that Rav
did not count it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is זעירי's case, the wife of his mother's father.

phrases.english: It can be confused by him
with the wife of his father's father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב מַאי טַעְמָא לָא חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the disagreement between רב and זעירי from רב's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב did not include the mother's father's wife among the cases with a הפסק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She could be confused with the father's father's wife, whose prohibition continues, so she is treated the same way.

steps.title: Why זעירי is not worried about confusion
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says there is no confusion: a person is often at his father's family's home, but not often at his mother's family's home, so he knows the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And זעירי? There he is often found going; here he is not often found going.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why זעירי does not share רב's worry, and answers that people know their father's family well, so they won't mix up the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a person visits his father's father's house often, he knows those relatives are forbidden. He will not confuse them with his mother's side, which he visits less. So for זעירי, the mother's father's wife can safely have a הפסק.

keyTerms.meaning: He is commonly found going there
To there: his father's father's home
To here: his mother's family's home

steps.whatToRemember: רב counts three שניות with a הפסק and worries that the mother's father's wife would be confused with the father's father's wife. זעירי adds her as the fourth, because people know their father's side well and won't mix them up.

phrases.english: And Ze'eiri?
phrases.notes: He means: why isn't זעירי worried about the mix-up that bothered רב?

phrases.english: To there he is commonly found going,
phrases.notes: 'There' is his father's father's home.

phrases.english: to here he is not commonly found going.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is his mother's family's home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives זעירי's side, answering the concern raised for רב in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why זעירי is not concerned that the two grandfathers' wives will be confused.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person regularly visits his father's family and knows they are forbidden, so he will not confuse them with his mother's side.

steps.title: Turning to the daughter-in-law case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes כלתו from רב's list to begin examining it.
steps.simpleTranslation: His daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up one item from רב's list, כלתו (his daughter-in-law), as a heading. It is setting up the next move, where it will look closely at this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled yet. The גמרא is going back to רב's list from step 32 and pointing to the daughter-in-law case so it can explain how the הפסק works there.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative forbidden מדרבנן, one step beyond the Torah's forbidden relatives
A stopping point, where the rabbinic prohibition does not continue further down the line

phrases.english: His daughter-in-law.
phrases.notes: This is the third case on רב's list from step 32. The גמרא now looks at it more closely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth about זעירי's added case, the גמרא returns to one of רב's original three cases to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heading line: כלתו, one of רב's שניות with a הפסק, is about to be explained.
